requirement: Describe VMNHU-003 as a Phase III, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 7-month study of intramuscular VM202 plus standard wound care versus placebo injections plus standard wound care in adults with diabetic nonhealing foot ulcers and peripheral arterial disease.

evidence.text: The title page and synopsis identify the Phase III randomized double-blind placebo-controlled multicenter design, population, intervention, control, and duration.
SAP Version E cites Protocol Version I and restates the seven-month parallel-group design.

requirement: State the planned 2:1 randomization to VM202 plus standard care versus placebo plus standard care and preserve randomized treatment assignment for efficacy analyses.

evidence.text: The synopsis specifies 200 VM202 and 100 placebo participants, and the analysis-set sections retain randomized assignment for efficacy.
The ITT and sensitivity efficacy populations are grouped by randomized assignment.

requirement: Report the protocol-planned total sample size of 300 participants, allocated 200 to VM202 and 100 to placebo, and preserve the distinction between this statistical plan and any later operational enrollment shortfall.

evidence.text: The protocol synopsis and sample-size section specify 300 participants in a 2:1 allocation.

requirement: Define the sole primary efficacy endpoint as the participant-level proportion with target-wound closure by the 4-month follow-up; define closure as 100% skin re-epithelialization without drainage or a dressing, and do not require the later 14 +/- 5 day confirmation for primary responder status.
acceptable_values: confirmation visit not required for primary response

evidence.text: Protocol Version I defines the primary 4-month closure endpoint and the separate 14 +/- 5 day confirmation endpoint.
The SAP explains that Version I removed confirmation from primary responder status and gives the complete-closure definition.

requirement: Define the ITT population as all randomized participants, analyze them according to randomized assignment regardless of treatment received, and use ITT for the primary analysis.

evidence.text: Protocol Version I defines ITT as all randomized participants analyzed by original assignment and binds it to the primary analysis.
SAP section 7.1 gives the same ITT definition and binding.

requirement: Define the Safety Population as randomized participants receiving at least one study injection, analyze them by actual treatment received, assign anyone receiving any VM202 to VM202 and participants never receiving VM202 to placebo, and use this set for all safety summaries.
acceptable_values: randomized and at least one injection

evidence.text: The safety-set section defines treated participants and actual-treatment attribution.
SAP section 7.2 repeats the definition and safety binding.

requirement: Define mITT as randomized participants who received study drug, have at least one postbaseline wound assessment, and have no predose safety or efficacy result that would retrospectively disqualify them after blinded CDRC review; analyze this set as randomized for primary-endpoint sensitivity analysis.

evidence.text: Protocol Version I defines all three mITT eligibility conditions and blinded adjudication.
SAP section 7.3 binds mITT to supportive primary-endpoint analysis.

requirement: Define PP1 as the mITT subset without protocol-prohibited medications or treatments that may affect wound healing, with use and effect adjudicated by the CDRC while blinded.
acceptable_values: no prohibited concomitant medication or treatment

evidence.text: Protocol section 6.2.4.1 defines PP1 and blinded CDRC review.
SAP section 7.4 carries the same PP1 definition.

requirement: Define PP2 as the PP1 subset meeting major eligibility criteria, receiving all assigned injections, maintaining required standard wound care, and satisfying any additional CDRC criteria fixed before unblinding; use PP1 and PP2 only as primary-endpoint sensitivity populations.

evidence.text: Protocol section 6.2.4.2 defines PP2 and assigns both PP sets to sensitivity analysis.
SAP section 7.4 repeats PP2 criteria and binding.

requirement: For the primary ITT comparison, apply Fisher's exact test, report each treatment group's responder rate with a binomial 95% confidence interval and the treatment-group rate difference with a 95% confidence interval, and classify an unassessable 4-month closure status as nonresponse.

evidence.text: SAP section 9.4.1.1 specifies the test, effect summaries, intervals, and nonresponder rule.

requirement: Support the primary result with an ITT logistic-regression analysis containing treatment as the main effect and reporting the VM202-versus-placebo odds ratio with a two-sided 95% Wald confidence interval, plus Fisher exact analyses in mITT, PP1, and PP2.
acceptable_values: Fisher exact in mITT and PP populations

evidence.text: SAP sections 9.4.1.2.1-9.4.1.2.2 define the supportive analyses.

requirement: Use a two-sided alpha of 0.05 for the one primary endpoint; make no multiplicity adjustment because there is one primary population and primary method, and label sensitivity and all other efficacy analyses supportive or exploratory rather than additional success claims.

evidence.text: The primary hypothesis and multiplicity section specify two-sided 0.05 and no multiplicity adjustment.

requirement: Cover the exploratory efficacy endpoints without promoting them to primary: time to closure; closure by 7 months; longitudinal wound volume, perimeter, area, and depth; new target-foot ulcers; time to major and minor target-limb amputation; ABI, TBI, and TcPO2 changes; and CWIQ quality-of-life change.

evidence.text: The protocol lists the nonprimary efficacy endpoints.
The SAP lists and analyzes the endpoints as exploratory.

requirement: Analyze time to complete closure and time to major or minor target-limb amputation with Kaplan-Meier estimates and log-rank treatment comparisons, censoring a participant without closure at end of study.

evidence.text: The endpoint derivation and analysis sections specify censoring, Kaplan-Meier summaries, and log-rank tests.

requirement: Analyze repeated percent changes in wound volume, perimeter, area, and depth with a linear mixed model containing treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, and the corresponding baseline value, initially using an unstructured covariance and selecting CS, AR(1), VC, or Toeplitz by corrected AIC if convergence fails.
acceptable_values: linear mixed model for repeated measures

evidence.text: SAP sections 9.4.4.3-9.4.4.4 specify the model terms, contrasts, covariance, and fallback selection.

requirement: For CWIQ, leave an overall-quality-of-life score missing when either underlying item is unanswered; within each three-domain score, replace missing items by that participant's mean of completed domain items only when less than 25% of the domain items are missing, otherwise leave the domain score missing.

evidence.text: SAP section 8.6.1 defines item-level CWIQ missing-data handling.

requirement: Analyze safety descriptively in the Safety Population by actual treatment, using available scheduled-visit data without imputing missing values; include exposure, injection-site events, adverse events, vital signs, HbA1c, chemistry, hematology, medications, retinal fundoscopy, and pharmacokinetic listings.

evidence.text: The protocol requires descriptive safety in treated participants with available data and no imputation.
SAP section 9.5 specifies the safety domains and summary conventions.

requirement: Define TEAEs as events starting after first dose or pre-existing conditions that worsen, conservatively classify an event as treatment-emergent when its first-dose-day start time or its start date is unknown, and summarize incidence and event counts by MedDRA SOC and preferred term, severity, relationship, injection, and protocol version.

evidence.text: SAP section 9.5.3 defines TEAEs, conservative unknown-date handling, and required summaries.

requirement: Record that the protocol-planned independent futility interim at 50% of dosed participants reaching month 4 was not conducted because enrollment stopped early; do not present the planned conditional-power rule as an analysis that occurred.

evidence.text: Protocol Version I describes the planned independent futility analysis and unchanged final alpha.
The final SAP states that early stopping prevented the protocol-specified interim analysis.

requirement: Ask the statistical team to confirm primary-endpoint intercurrent-event strategies beyond the stated 4-month assessment rule and to supply the detailed futility boundary or conditional-power decision rule before making either operationally binding; do not invent these SAP-level choices from the protocol synopsis.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies analysis sets and a planned interim but delegates detailed interim implementation and does not provide a complete estimand strategy.

notes: The later early stopping and nonexecution of the interim remain confirmed-decision context rather than hidden protocol-only facts.

requirement: For the final analysis context, state that only 44 participants enrolled—7 under protocol C, 5 under E, 16 under F, and 16 under G, with none under D, H, or I—and keep this observed enrollment separate from the protocol-planned sample of 300.
acceptable_values: none under D H or I

evidence.text: The SAP enumerates enrollment by protocol version, totaling 44 participants.

notes: Observed enrollment is a confirmed-decision context item and must not be scored as a hidden protocol-only fact.
